LESSON: READING 6.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY (CLASS READER)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story (Class Reader), part of Strand 6 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do people read short stories?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a prescribed section of the short story,

2. discuss the storyline,

3. present findings in a talking tree,

4. summarise the main idea in the short story,

5. act out a section of the short story, with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a prescribed section of the short story,
2. discuss the storyline,
3. present findings in a talking tree,
4. summarise the main idea in the short story,
5. act out a section of the short story, with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: It is enriched as the learner shares what they have learnt through a presentation.

Values:
Unity: It is strengthened as the learner demonstrates team spirit while engaging in a group discussion on the storyline.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Gender roles: These are underscored as the learner identifies gender roles highlighted in the short story and relates them to real

life.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner relates the concepts in short stories to reading short stories in Kiswahili.
